newsitem.title: USA: NEES says shuts 400 MW Mass. power unit.
newsitem.headline: NEES says shuts 400 MW Mass. power unit.

text.p: New England Electric System said Tuesday that an oil-fired generating unit at its Salem, Massachusetts power plant was shut today due to a tube leak but the unit was expected back early Wednesday.

"At our Salem Harbor plant, unit four had a tube leak. It's a routine repair and it should be back by 6 A.M. (0600 EDT)," said Susan Stevens, director of corporate communications, adding the unit had a capacity of 400 megawatts (MW).
Stevens also said two units at the company's Brayton Point plant in Somerset, Mass., had motor problems and were operating at reduced capacity.
"Units one and two at our Brayton Point plant had motor problems and are operating at 50 percent. Those should be back by the end of the week," she said, adding each unit had a capacity of 250 MWs.
Coal is the primary source of fuel at the Brayton Point plant, with oil used as a backup.

"We're expecting another hot, humid day here again tomorrow and NEPOOL (New England Power Pool) has declared tomorrow a conservation day," Stevens said, explaining the regional grid operator has asked customers to voluntarily cut back on electric usage Wednesday.
